findings.summary: Taking every unit-matching figure on a judged line sends correct work back, because real status lines print comparison figures in the same unit.
findings.evidence: throughput.rs:794 appends `; the {n} landings before: {figure}` to the USD and percent lines. For example `spent on attempts that did not land: 1.23 USD over the last 5 landing(s); the 5 landings before: 0.40 USD` and `landed on the first attempt: 60% …; the 5 landings before: 20%`. The build-wait line is `build wait {total} s over {n} check(s), longest {longest} s` (831-833). Under the plan's rule, a usage-measure criterion naming `spent on attempts that did not land` with range 1 to 2 USD would judge 0.40 USD as out of range and spend the shared send-back. The same happens for `build wait` with `longest`. The real-text test only exercises `idle between jobs`, `landing time` and `throughput`, so it would not catch this. Fix: Take only the first figure in the range's unit family that follows the measure phrase on the judged line (after the colon if there is one). Ignore figures after a `;` or inside parentheses unless they form the per-item list. Add unit tests on the real USD, percent (with `the N landings before`) and build-wait lines, asserting that only the current figure is judged.
findings.location: Plan Approach step 4 (Figures rule) and Decision 1/5; crates/athena-core/src/status/throughput.rs:792-805, 830-834

findings.summary: The per-item branch would flag equal stage medians as constant, which contradicts the plan's own test. 'Three or more equal items' also differs from the request's 'same answer for every item'.
findings.evidence: `named()` returns six stages (reading, planning, producer, checks, verifier, landing and rebuild). They are printed as `({name} {m:.1} · …)` on the `median per landed job` line. These labels are not dates. So by Decision 2, a criterion that says 'for each job' or 'per job', and whose phrase matches this line, makes three or more equal stage values (planning, checks and landing are often 0.0) a 'constant' problem. Yet step 7 and Decision 2 claim a unit test showing equal stage medians with per-item wording give no problem. The rule as written cannot pass that test. Also, 'Three or more equal items are a problem' can be read as any three equal values among more items, but the request says the same answer for every item. Fix: Drop the per-item-wording branch and judge constants only on lists whose labels are job ids. Or also require labels that are job ids or item ids rather than words. State that 'constant' means every item in the list is equal, with at least three items. Keep the stage-median test with per-item wording and make the rule satisfy it.
findings.location: Plan Approach step 4 (Items rule), Decision 2, and the Step 7 unit test 'equal stage medians with and without per-item wording'; throughput.rs:113-121, 806-812

findings.summary: The constant rule depends on an output format that `status --snapshot` does not print today, so on current output it can never fire.
findings.evidence: Real throughput text (throughput.rs:836-844) prints medians and totals, with no parenthesised per-job list labelled by job ids. Demonstrations 1-3 use an invented `landing time 4.0 min (20261101-… 3.0 · …)` line. The failure the gate itself cites (a landing time of 0.1 minutes for every job, surveys.rs:591) appears in the real output only as one median. The open question covers only the missing numeric range, not this. Fix: Say in D183, the CHANGELOG and the open question that a constant can only be caught when the output prints a per-job list labelled by job ids. Ask whether Athena should instead compute per-item values from the snapshot, or whether that limit is acceptable.
findings.location: Open questions; Risks bullet 2; D183 content

findings.summary: Mapping every `status --snapshot` command to `cargo run -p athena-cli` assumes the job's repository is Athena's own.
findings.evidence: The gate applies to RECORDS_MEASURE_PATHS (surveys.rs:410-413), which are Athena source files, so in practice this holds. But selection only matches on the text `status --snapshot` and `real records`, so it is not tied to that repository. Fix: Also gate selection on the repository having an `athena-cli` package, or on the change touching RECORDS_MEASURE_PATHS. Otherwise state in the module docs that elsewhere the run is recorded as `not run`.
findings.location: Approach step 1 / Decision 6 (command mapping to `cargo run -p athena-cli`)

summary: Round 3. The plan matches the request and the accepted reading. The places it names exist: producer.rs:507-527 (loop_check_failures, then `break Some(report)`), the SnapExec `in_loop` executor (checks.rs:73-162), demo_seam and demo_runs_here (checks.rs:557-615), `evaluate(policy, tool, input, cwd)` and `Policy.evidence` (policy.rs:35-90), evidence_dir, read_history and unlock in snapshot.rs, and `evidence_placeholder` = `<state>/jobs/{job}/evidence` (briefs.rs:651). `CheckResultView` derives Default, and every builder I found uses `..Default::default()` or is listed in the dependents. The stored-form rule, choice (b) for the verdict, and the reuse of the in-loop executor all hold up. Two problems remain, both in the judging rules, when checked against the text `status` really prints (status/throughput.rs:789-845). (1) The rule "every number on a judged line followed by a unit in the range's family" also takes comparison figures that real lines print in the same unit. Examples: `; the N landings before: X USD`, the same pattern with `%`, and `build wait … s …, longest … s`. Correct work would be sent back because an earlier window's figure, or the longest wait, falls outside the range. (2) The per-item rule ("per job" wording, at least three items, no date labels) would call six equal stage medians (`reading 0.0 · planning 0.0 · …`) constant. That contradicts the plan's own unit test, which asserts no problem for equal stage medians when the criterion has per-item wording. "Three or more equal items" also differs from the request's "the same answer for every item". The plan can fix both, so the verdict is revise.
